title: Rampwave orchestrator and slowpath injector for tail-latency faulting
author: Priya Mehta
release_notes: Adds a new orchestrator that creates staged ramp-up waveforms and an optional slowpath injector to reproduce tail latency events for profiling. Includes CLI and YAML workload descriptions, new reporters for p99+/tail attribution, and a baseline scenario for CI regression checks.
description:
Context and motivation: We regularly see production tail events that are hard to reproduce in the benchmark lab because standard steady-state generators do not create correlated bursts with staggered cache states. This PR introduces a Rampwave Orchestrator that composes multiple cohort-based waves (staggered ramps + decay) to exercise cache warmups, kernel cold-paths, and scheduler contention. It also adds an optional Slowpath Injector that programmatically forces slow-path code paths (file I/O fallbacks, simulated memory pressure hooks, and deliberate KV cache miss storms) to reliably surface tail phenomena for profiling and root-cause attribution.

What this changes: single continuous explanation of the primary changes and rationale: 1) rampwave/orchestrator module: new scheduler that accepts a YAML workload manifest with named cohorts, per-cohort arrival curves (linear/ramp/exponential), and priming offsets to exercise prefix cache coverage. 2) slowpath/injector module: pluggable hooks that can be enabled per-cohort; supported hooks include kv_miss_burst, simulated_io_block, and tokenize-slowpath. 3) reporters: a tail-attribution reporter that correlates p95/p99+/p999 spikes with active cohorts, hook events, and kernel tags; output format is newline-delimited JSON for downstream aggregation. 4) CI baseline: a new deterministic scenario (rampwave-small) added to the perf-suite which runs on PRs to detect regressions in tail metrics. 5) examples and docs: workload manifests and a shortguide to design rampwave experiments.

Commits summary: (high-level) - 7c1a2d7: add orchestrator scheduler and YAML manifest parser - 9f3b4ee: implement slowpath injector hooks and runtime toggles - d2a8b5c: tail-attribution reporter and NLJSON formatter - 3a44f1b: add deterministic rampwave CI scenario and test harness - 4f2e3d0: examples, docs, and small refactors for shared load abstractions

Files changed (high level): - benchmark_lab/orchestrator/rampwave.py - benchmark_lab/slowpath/injector.py - benchmark_lab/reporters/tail_attribution.py - perf-ci/scenarios/rampwave-small.yaml - examples/rampwave-manifests/basic-staggered.yaml - docs/perf/rampwave.md - tests/perf/test_rampwave_ci.py - small edits to common workload utilities and README

Testing and CI: The PR initially failed one flaky integration test (test_cohort_alignment) on the first run due to timing assumptions in the harness; I adjusted the harness to use deterministic simulated time for the CI scenario and re-ran. Final CI: 18 checks passed (unit, lint, mypy, integration with simulated time, perf smoke), 2 manual checks (doc review, release-note) marked complete. The ci_status is "pass after rerun".

Review conversation snapshot: Reviewer Kai: "Nice API for defining cohorts — please add an example that demonstrates a burst followed by a slow decay. Also add a unit test that asserts cohort priming offsets are applied correctly." Author (Priya): "Added basic-staggered.yaml and unit test test_cohort_offsets in tests/perf. I also switched the CI scenario to use simulated time to avoid flakes." Reviewer Rebecca: "Slowpath hooks look powerful; can we gate the I/O hook behind an explicit flag to avoid accidental use in shared infra?" Author: "Done — slowpath I/O is behind --enable-slowpath-io and documented in rampwave.md." Reviewer Samir: "Can you add a short section on interpreting the tail-attribution output and a sample dash import?" Author: "Added interpretation appendix and a sample Kibana ingest script in docs." Approvals: Kai approved after small nits were addressed; Rebecca approved; Samir requested one follow-up issue for extended kvcache instrumentation (ENG-4514) and gave approval.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Post-merge actions: created a Linear task ENG-4514 to extend kvcache instrumentation and ENG-4515 to add a scheduled nightly rampwave-large run for long-tail monitoring.

Notes and guidance for future use: Use the rampwave YAML manifests to create reproducible cohort mixes. When investigating tails in CI, enable the slowpath injector hooks selectively and run with the p99 attribution reporter enabled. The new reporter includes per-cohort counters and kernel tag attribution to make root-cause handoffs to runtime engineers easier.
